content.value_statement: Large JavaScript repositories can suffer from slow builds, duplicated tooling, and unclear package boundaries. This skill provides practical Turborepo, Nx, and pnpm workspace patterns for maintainable monorepos.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use monorepos and how to structure apps, packages, and shared configuration.
Provides Turborepo setup examples for builds, tests, linting, type checks, caching, and development tasks.
Shows pnpm workspace configuration and package filtering for dependency management.
Documents Nx workspace setup, affected commands, dependency graphs, and parallel task execution.
Covers shared TypeScript, ESLint, UI, utility, and type package patterns.
Outlines CI workflows, affected deployments, and package publishing with changesets.
limitations: The skill is a guide and does not execute commands or generate a full repository automatically.
Examples focus on JavaScript and TypeScript ecosystems, not polyglot enterprise monorepos.
Tool versions in examples may need updates for a specific project.
Access control, governance, and compliance policy design require separate review.

use_cases.title: Set Up a New Workspace
use_cases.description: Create an initial monorepo layout with apps, packages, shared configs, task pipelines, and package manager settings.

use_cases.title: Improve Build Performance
use_cases.description: Tune task dependencies, cache inputs, cache outputs, affected commands, and parallel execution for faster feedback.

use_cases.title: Plan a Repository Migration
use_cases.description: Map existing repositories into packages, define shared dependencies, and prepare CI workflows for a gradual move.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Monorepo Tool
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose between Turborepo, Nx, and pnpm workspaces for a TypeScript product with two apps and shared UI packages.

prompt_templates.title: Design Package Structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a monorepo structure for apps/web, apps/docs, packages/ui, packages/config, and packages/types. Include package boundaries and scripts.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Task Pipelines
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my monorepo task pipeline and suggest cache inputs, outputs, dependencies, and affected commands for build, test, lint, and type-check.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Migration and Release Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a phased migration plan from separate repositories to a pnpm monorepo with shared packages, CI, affected deploys, and changeset releases.

output_examples.input: I need a monorepo layout for a web app, docs site, shared UI library, and shared TypeScript config.
output: Recommended layout with apps and packages separated by ownership and release needs.
Root tasks for build, test, lint, development, and type checks.
Shared configuration packages for TypeScript, linting, and UI conventions.

output_examples.input: Our monorepo builds everything on each pull request and feedback is slow.
output: Use affected project detection before build, test, and deployment steps.
Define precise cache inputs and outputs for generated artifacts.
Run independent package tasks in parallel while preserving dependency order.

output_examples.input: We want to publish shared packages from a monorepo.
output: Use a release process that records package changes before publishing.
Keep package ownership and versioning rules documented in each package.
Store publishing credentials in CI secrets with limited scope.

best_practices: Keep package boundaries clear and avoid circular dependencies between shared packages.
Centralize common TypeScript, linting, formatting, and testing configuration.
Configure cache inputs and outputs so CI only repeats work that changed.
anti_patterns: Do not share every utility by default when local ownership would be simpler.
Do not rely on phantom dependencies that are missing from each package manifest.
Do not publish packages without a documented versioning and release strategy.

faq.question: Does this skill create a monorepo automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance, examples, and planning support for building or improving a monorepo.

faq.question: Which tools does the skill focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on Turborepo, Nx, pnpm workspaces, shared configuration, CI, caching, and package publishing.

faq.question: Can I use it with npm or Yarn workspaces?
faq.answer: Yes, but most detailed workspace examples use pnpm because it is the recommended package manager in the guide.

faq.question: Is this useful for existing repositories?
faq.answer: Yes. It can help plan migrations, shared package design, and CI changes for existing projects.

faq.question: Does it cover security policy for monorepos?
faq.answer: Only at a basic level. Access control, secret handling, and compliance need separate security review.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
